en: The Candra-sūtra. 1. Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery.
2. At that time, the entire lunar disc was eclipsed by Rāhu, the lord of the asuras.

3. Then the deity who dwelt in that lunar disk, being afraid, terrified, agitated, and with the hair on her body standing on end, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One, she stood to one side. Standing to one side, that deity at that time spoke these verses:
Ed. reads *bhitā*, but the manuscript (MS) reads *bhītā*: "O Heroic Buddha, homage be to you who are liberated in every way; I have fallen into great distress—be my refuge."
O Buddha, hero, Arhat, Sugata, the moon in this world has gone for refuge;
O Buddhas who have compassion for the worlds, release the moon from Rāhu!
6. The Blessed One said:
O Rāhu, do not swallow in the midst of the sky that dispeller of darkness, the maker of light, the radiant one of pure white splendor—the moon, the lamp of all creatures; release him quickly!
7. Then the asura lord Rāhu very quickly released the lunar disk;
hurrying thereafter, that Rāhu let go of the moon, his limbs perspiring, distressed, agitated, and as if afflicted.
8. Bali Vairocana saw that the lunar disk had been very swiftly released by Rāhu, the lord of the asuras. Having seen this, Bali spoke this verse:
Why indeed do you, Rāhu, release the moon in such haste,
with your limbs perspiring, distressed, agitated, and as if afflicted?
Cf. Pelliot Sanskrit bleu 449 Ac: /// [a]ro yathā //
10. Rāhu said:
May my head split into seven pieces, and may I find no happiness while living, if I do not release the moon by means of this verse sung by the Buddha.
Rāhu said: "May my head split into seven pieces..."
11. Baḍir Vairocana said:
"For those who see [the truth] through the singing of verses, Rāhu releases the moon."
Cf. Pelliot Sanskrit bleu 449 Ad: + + + + + .. .. .. .. .. .. (bh)i(g)itena muñce 12. The Candrasūtra is completed.
